answer: Edge-Diversity Weighting. An agent's influence is scaled by the entropy of distinct routes its messages traverse, giving a signal that costs attackers to fake. A cluster confined to one short horizon of the graph scores near zero regardless of node count, since routing must fan across independent relay neighborhoods. Costs stay hidden until a probe forces a wide crystal of disjoint paths to hold. Each Sybil identity therefore pays full routing overhead per broadcast, not a cheap shared shortcut.
